title: review: G9 fix round 3: pool.codex_available takes the task too, so availability and dispatch routing agree (review T-0325)
spec:
STEP 0: the worktree must contain 5ebe137 "Pass execute task to executor routing" over ad6bdf2 and 8a84cfa in git log; never drop them.
Review T-0325 on T-0314 (med): pool.codex_available() still calls pick_executor("execute", complexity) without task=, so status(), pool.status() and the daemon's cooling notice can report an executor available via generic scores while executor.start()'s task-aware routing picks a different or no executor for the same task; acceptance 3 of T-0314 (grep shows no production pick_executor call for execute tasks lacking task=) still fails on that line.
Change: pool.codex_available(complexity, task=None) passes task through to pick_executor; every caller that has a task passes it (executor.start, daemon cooling notice if it has one); callers without a task keep the generic answer. Test: tests/test_pool.py::test_codex_available_uses_task_routing (with a task whose class routes to a specific executor, codex_available agrees with pick_executor). Keep every existing test green.
acceptance: git log --oneline in the worktree shows 5ebe137, ad6bdf2 and 8a84cfa below your commit
grep -n 'pick_executor(' orchestrator/*.py shows task= on every execute-role call
Existing tests pass; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 in the worktree

comments.issue: status() now calls _expected_costs() per executor, fanning out to scorecard.expected_cost() for each of the 5 TASK_CLASSES; each call does an uncached full scan of runs/*.jsonl and tasks/T-*.json. Since status() is polled by the daemon loop, cli, and mcp tool, this multiplies an already O(n) scan by executors×classes on every poll and will scale worse as history grows. Not blocking (not in acceptance criteria, no correctness impact) but worth caching/memoizing per status() call.
